data.title: Elon Musk Is ‘Okay With Being Disliked’ — and He Knows Exactly Where His $985 Billion Fortune Is Going
data.description:
Elon Musk is the world’s richest person, currently worth nearly $1 trillion, a milestone he became the first to hit earlier this year. Musk is also the most followed person on social media platform X with more than 240 million followers.

Here’s what Musk wants his legacy to be and where his money should go after he passes.

Musk on Being Liked

In a new interview with author Walter Isaacson, Musk covers his thoughts on key topics like artificial intelligence and more. He also shares details about his personal life and ideals, similar to what Isaacson wrote in a biography of the billionaire several years ago.

"Sometimes I don’t like to be liked," Musk said. "I’m okay with being disliked."

Musk told Isaacson on "The Builders" podcast that wanting to be liked could be a bad quality for building a company, as things may not work out if you are doing things that diminish the success rate of the company in order to be liked.

While Musk recognizes that many people don’t like him, he highlights his large social media following and predicts that, among people who know who he is, 70% to 80% like him.

"Some people hate my guts."

Musk’s Legacy

Musk has plenty of thoughts on how AI and robots could create universal income and wealth for everyone and make money obsolete. If that happens, his current $985 billion net worth could be changed.

"The future is going to be AI and robots," Musk said.

He said currency won’t matter someday. "I don’t think money’s going to matter in the future."

If money does matter and Musk remains the richest person, he said that his descendants will have a high tax bill and may be worth less than he is.

The billionaire said most of his net worth will go towards his foundation and help preserve his legacy. Asked what he hopes his legacy will be, Musk hit on three key ideals.

The billionaire wants his wealth to "continue the goals" of making life multi-planetary, extend consciousness to the stars and improve sustainability on Earth.

data.title: FCA Proposes Crypto Crime Guidance On Wallet Checks And Blockchain Analytics
data.description:
TL;DR: The FCA is consulting on updated financial crime guidance for crypto businesses, including customer checks, blockchain analytics and the Travel Rule. Responses are due December 24, and the guide itself would not create new rules.

Crypto businesses preparing for the UK’s expanded regulatory regime have a more detailed picture of the controls the Financial Conduct Authority expects them to build.

The regulator’s October 23 consultation proposes changes to its Financial Crime Guide, covering cryptoassets alongside fraud, sanctions, data security and money laundering. The proposals apply to the FCA’s financial crime supervisory population, including cryptoasset businesses and firms overseen under the Money Laundering Regulations.

The practical focus is on how firms assess customers and transactions, and how they react when risk changes. A blockchain record can help an investigation, but a record alone does not decide whether a customer explanation is credible or a transfer needs further scrutiny.

Analytics Must Sit Inside A Working Control System

The consultation paper proposes examples of good and poor practice for enhanced due diligence, onboarding and transaction monitoring. It specifically addresses the use of blockchain analytics and further guidance on the Travel Rule, which concerns information accompanying certain transfers.

The paper also reminds firms that governance must evolve as their businesses grow. Its proposed changes include a question about whether policies and staff training distinguish obligations under proceeds-of-crime legislation from those under terrorism legislation.

For an exchange or provider of custody, the implication is that buying a screening product is only one part of the job. Someone still has to set its thresholds, review alerts and document decisions. A technically accurate warning is of limited use if it sits unreviewed while funds move elsewhere.

That matters for stablecoin transfers as much as for volatile tokens. A stable unit price does not establish the identity of a sender or the origin of funds. Transaction risk and market risk are different questions, and control systems need to reflect that distinction.

Guidance Now, A Wider Regime In 2027

The FCA says the guide contains no rules and imposes no new requirements. It is intended to help firms understand supervisory expectations and assess their own arrangements. The consultation closes on December 24, after which the regulator plans to publish feedback and the final text in a policy statement.

Separately, the FCA’s regime overview says the wider cryptoasset framework is expected to begin on October 25, 2027. Applications for authorization are already open, and the regulator published a package of final rules in June.

The distinction between those stages matters for firms planning investment in compliance. This consultation does not postpone existing anti-money-laundering duties until next year, nor does it bring the whole future regime into force immediately. It fills in the proposed guidance firms can use when translating their obligations into day-to-day decisions.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: SA Asks: How much could Tesla be worth in a merger deal?
data.description:
On Tuesday, Elon Musk revealed that Tesla and SpaceX have established committees to explore a merger combination.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Danil Sereda, Victor Dergunov, and Carla Magliocco how much they thought Tesla could be worth in a merger deal.

Danil Sereda: There are actually many moving parts here. Usually, boards establish independent special committees to determine the price. Musk said the companies had already formed special committees, so I'd expect the merger to close within the next year or two.

We know that Tesla produces positive operating cash flow (>$18B on a TTM basis, per Seeking Alpha). It also holds ~$43.5B in liquid cash and investments, whereas SpaceX burned over $42B in CapEx on a TTM basis (mainly on its orbital infrastructure and AI-related stuff). So I agree with some analysts who say that Tesla shareholders might be willing to take >50% control of the combined entity (that's an assumption from Morningstar).

I'll take 50% here to account for SPCX's structurally higher valuation at the start because it has more growth pillars. At 50% of the combined market cap right now (~$3.5T), I'm getting to $1.75T for TSLA, which has ~3.95B diluted shares outstanding. This gives me a fair value per share of $443, which is around 20% above today's price (I'm comparing to the pre-market price of ~$368/share on Thursday, Oct. 22). Of course, the proportion might be above 50% for Tesla, and in that case, the premium will be higher.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

Victor Dergunov: I think SpaceX would pay $420 to $500 per share at the very least for Tesla , and that is if the deal went through in the very near term. However, the high-interest environment may push the deal to mid-2027 or so. It's possible the markets may be more optimistic because of easier Fed policy by then, and I'd prefer $550 or more for my shares, as it is my portfolio's most considerable position. I also want to increase my position on any pullbacks in Tesla's stock in future weeks and months.

Carla Magliocco: In an article I wrote in May about Tesla and its vertical integration, a user asked me how the IPO of SpaceX , which took place the following month, would affect Tesla . There were plenty of doubts about it, and it was believed that Tesla investors would sell their shares and rush toward SpaceX . But none of that happened.

So, at that moment, my answer was yes, I'd love a merger because it would unite all the potential of the physical AI that Tesla was already developing. Since at least 2023, Musk has said he wanted to base his corporate ecosystem on AI. And I believe that makes sense.

In the preview of Q3 that I wrote about Tesla earlier this week, I explained that the FSD model is precisely that: a platform that builds an empire of physical AI. In the preview, I estimated 1.62M active subscribers, but I fell short: there were 1.74M, representing 67% year-over-year growth.

But now, such a merger would benefit even more the sentiment of Tesla investors, and as I own shares of Tesla and not SpaceX , this really excites me. But it's more about a mutual benefit. SpaceX just showed in its Q3 results that its Super Intelligence segment is not only growing more than expected but is also reaching higher profitability.

Meanwhile, Tesla still doesn't show strong profitability, and that's why it needs more investment to accelerate the production of Robotaxis and Optimus and reach a more advanced FSD system without supervision. At the same time, Tesla would give SpaceX what SpaceX doesn't have: monetization of its physical AI. Therefore, I believe that any news about a merger would make Tesla rise, although the final result will depend on the terms.

data.title: Silver Price Analysis as October Sell-Off Tests the Market’s Recovery Prospects
data.description:
The swift drop in silver prices in October has put the precious metal at a pivotal level, and the metal has dropped by almost 6% over the last week.

Silver Extends Its October Decline as Selling Pressure Builds

The supplied Trading Economics chart shows silver prices dropping 5.96% for the week to $53.883 per ounce.The weekly chang show-3.412. The prices were again hovering around $53.9 on October 24, and the chart was indicating a big pullback from above $57 earlier this week.

The drop further escalated since October 22, when silver breached the $56 level and headed down to $54. Source: TradingEconomics

The price closed in the mid-$50s, before stabilising a fraction of a penny higher. The chart displays a brief period of consolidation late in the week; however, this is not yet a confirmation of a longer-term reversal.

Further market commentary also highlights yield pressures, a stronger US dollar and interest-rate expectations. On October 23, FOREX.com news agency said that silver had found a long-term support base of 50-55 after a wide precious-metals sell-off.

TradingView Signals Point to a Weak Technical Structure

As of October 24, silver was trading at $53.918 on the provided TradingView chart, which had declined by 1.26% during the session. The displayed moving averages were at $61.309 and $63.618, respectively, which were still above the price. Both were on a downward trend, suggesting that prices in recent times have been subdued during the considered time periods.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) was at 31.58, which is below the average level of 38.21. The latest reading puts silver near the 30 level, which is typically seen as oversold. Source: TradingView

But this isn't a conclusive sign of recovery, especially if the prices continue in the form of lower lows. The first important area of the technical zone is the interval between $53 and $55. Any continuation of the trend below $53 would leave the market open for more losses to the $50 price level.

On the other hand, a recovery above $55 will signal an initial stabilisation. However, with more evidence of a change in trend, silver would need to reach higher levels and test resistance at $61-$64.

These levels are technical levels that you are given in this chart and NOT guaranteed future trading levels. A change in the price action may be in sight, depending on the direction of US Treasury yields, the dollar and the general sentiment on precious metals.

October and December Forecasts rely on a Market Reversal.

October and December Forecasts Depend on a Market Reversal

However, the charts are looking for caution for the rest of the month as silver is still trading below its period averages. A break above $55 would signal a short-term recovery, while a drop below $53 would increase downside risk. The 50-55 zone continues to be significant as market analysts have found it to be a wider support area.

December is a more ambiguous month. In the August forecast, J.P. Morgan had an average of $63/oz. for Q4 and $70.60/oz. for 2026. The forecast aligned with expectations of easing physical-market tightness, declining industrial demand, and interest-rate pressures. These are average which are forecasts and do not guarantee December closing prices.

On X, Rashad Hajiyev stated that silver has formed a long-term cup and handle breakout and retest. Prices may even reach $200 by 2027, he said. Source: X Via Rashad

This, of course, is an analyst's bull case and not a market consensus or actual projection. Buyers would have needed to take control and break out of the technical resistance near $60–$63 to make a move in December.

A continued lacklustre performance may instead drag silver down to around $50–$55. The evidence provided herein suggests that the next few months are a period of caution until prices recover and cross key moving averages, but the longer-term trend depends on monetary policy, industrial demand and investment flows.

data.title: New York Seeks $1.3 Billion From NovaTech Founders In Crypto Fraud Case
data.description:
TL;DR: New York’s attorney general is seeking $1.3 billion in monetary relief in the NovaTech case and has announced nearly $6 million in promoter settlements. The larger sum is a request to the court, not money recovered for investors.

New York’s effort to recover losses from the NovaTech cryptocurrency scheme has reached a new stage, with Attorney General Letitia James asking a court to impose roughly $1.3 billion in damages and disgorgement.

The October 22 announcement also disclosed nearly $6 million in settlements with four promoters. Those are separate from the much larger claim involving founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion. The announcement does not establish that either amount has already reached victims.

The case concerns investment packages sold through NovaTech and an earlier business, AWS Mining. According to the attorney general, the schemes targeted Haitian and other immigrant communities through religious networks, social media and messaging groups.

The New Filing Follows An Earlier Judgment

An affirmation filed on October 22 supports the request for monetary relief. It records that New York sued in June 2024 and that the defaulting defendants did not respond or appear. The court entered a default order and judgment on August 4, 2025.

The latest motion asks the court to determine the financial consequences. It should not be confused with a new criminal conviction, a completed recovery or a guarantee that a judgment can be collected. Those distinctions are particularly important when the sums sought are much larger than the settlements announced alongside them.

The promoter figures listed by the attorney general are $2.9 million from Martin Zizi, $2.05 million from Frantz Ciceron, $750,000 from James Corbett and $275,861 from Ricardo Roy Sr. All four face permanent bans from the securities, commodities and cryptocurrency industries.

The timing also needs care: the Zizi consent papers were filed in November 2025. This week’s announcement brings the settlement figures together; it does not mean every agreement was signed this week.

Recruitment Promises Outran The Trading Business

The original mining operation offered high returns and recruiting bonuses, according to the court affirmation. NovaTech later marketed cryptocurrency trading packages. The cryptocurrency label described how investors supplied money, but the underlying issue was what operators actually did with it.

That is a useful distinction for readers assessing similar pitches. An account balance on a website does not establish that assets exist, that trades occurred or that withdrawals can be honored. Nor does a familiar community connection answer questions about custody and control of funds.

For affected investors, the next substantive development will be the court’s decision on monetary relief and any subsequent recovery process. The announced settlements and the requested award address different defendants and different steps in that process; combining them into a headline recovery figure would overstate what has happened.

Related reading: How crypto exchanges work.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Forget Anthropic: Biotech Is Quietly Dominating the IPO Sphere — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Paul R. La Monica

The initial public offering market has been in a lull as investors continue to wait for Claude developer Anthropic to officially file a S-1 form, with a handful of companies making their public debuts in recent weeks. Just don't tell that to biotech investors.

Five biotechs have gone public this month, and several of them have soared — including Lycia Therapeutics, which gained 67% on Friday. Lycia, which is developing drugs for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases as well as food allergies, priced its offering at $18, the high end of its range, and sold $314 million in stock in its IPO Friday. Shares closed the session at $30 but at one point, Lycia stock had more than doubled, reaching a peak of $36.49.

Lycia's IPO follows the healthy debut for City Therapeutics, a biotech that is working on drugs to treat degenerative eye condition Stargardt disease and some blood clotting disorders. City, which has partnerships with Bausch + Lomb and Biogen and counts Fidelity as a notable investor, rose nearly 30% on its first day of trading on Oct. 16. The stock has pulled back a bit since then, but is still 15% above its IPO price.

Retension Pharmaceuticals, which is developing drugs to treat high blood pressure, is up 27% since it went public on Oct. 9. In a sign that demand for the IPO was strong, Retension increased the size of the stock sale to 3.8 million shares from an original plan of 3.3 million.

Two other biotechs have made their Wall Street debuts this month, but haven't fared as well. TRex Bio, which is also working on autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, has dropped about 1% since its Oct. 8 IPO. Iambic Therapeutics, despite a 18% gain on its first day of trading on Oct. 15, is now down more than 10% from its IPO price.

Iambic, which is using AI to develop drugs to treat various forms of cancer, is backed by Cathie Wood's ARK Investment Management, Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office and Nvidia.

None of these five companies are profitable. as all are early-stage biotechs. But the fact that they have been able to make it through the IPO window at a time when other companies, such as smart ring maker Oura and Solidigm, the flash memory unit of South Korean AI chip company SK Hynix, have shelved their planned listings, is a promising sign that investors still have an appetite for some start-ups.

"Healthcare remains a bright spot," wrote Bill Smith, CEO and founder of IPO research and investing firm Renaissance Capital in a recent report. To that end, several other biotechs, including Aspen Neuroscience and Bambusa Therapeutics, filed for IPOs this month.

Still, the broader IPO market may remain in hibernation for at least another month. Smith said money companies are preferring to stay on the sideline "as most issuers wait to get past the current volatility, the midterms, and the Anthropic IPO."

A draft of Anthropic's IPO filing shows the company lost more than $80 billion in the first half of 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported. Even though more than $70 billion of that is said to be due to accounting charges, some investors may be reluctant to pay a premium for the company.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

The weak performance of other recent IPOs, like those of sandwich chain Jersey Mike's Subs and homeowners insurer Orion180, doesn't help, either. But for now, it looks like biotech investors are ignoring the IPO doldrums.

Write to Paul R. La Monica at paul.lamonica@barrons.com

data.title: SEC Puts Tokenization On Its 2027 Examination Agenda
data.description:
TL;DR: The SEC has named tokenization among its fiscal 2027 examination priorities, bringing the systems behind blockchain securities into closer supervisory focus. The staff document sets inspection priorities and creates no new legal obligations.

The SEC’s tokenization agenda now includes a practical question for financial firms: can the infrastructure work reliably when something goes wrong?

In its October 23 announcement, the US regulator placed tokenization among the market developments its examiners will scrutinize during fiscal 2027. The wider program also covers investment advice, complex products, private credit and cybersecurity across more than 34,000 registrants.

For companies building services around tokenized assets, that brings the discussion down from the promise of faster trading to the controls supporting it. A share recorded on a blockchain still needs dependable ownership records, functioning markets and an orderly response to disruption.

Clearing And Trading Systems Enter The Frame

The 20-page examination document explicitly includes tokenization among high-risk areas for clearing-agency reviews. In its discussion of Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity, it lists tokenized securities alongside extended trading hours, advanced AI and quantum computing. Cloud providers and other technology suppliers also feature in those reviews.

That combination matters. Extending trading hours can leave less time for maintenance, while connecting a token to conventional securities records adds another place where systems must agree. The relevant test is whether the complete service remains dependable, including the handoffs between systems.

The document separately emphasizes cybersecurity governance, access controls, incident response and risks from shared technology. It also states that the priorities are staff views, carry no legal force and do not amend existing law. An examination focus should therefore be read as a signal about supervision, rather than a new tokenization license or prohibition.

A Permission To Experiment Still Comes With Conditions

The context is the SEC’s September innovation exemption for certain tokenized stock venues. That temporary framework requires equivalent shareholder rights, issuer notification and an opportunity to object when an unaffiliated party tokenizes shares. It also imposes trading limits and requirements for public, auditable smart contracts.

Those conditions illustrate why market access and operational supervision move together. A permitted venue can still have weak controls; a technically impressive platform can still mishandle an investor’s rights. The new priorities put attention on that gap.

For investors, the useful distinction is between the token and the service built around it. Questions about who holds the underlying security, how transactions reconcile and what happens during an outage remain relevant alongside the blockchain’s design. Custody and market infrastructure do not become incidental simply because a trade uses a token.

The SEC says its priorities are non-exhaustive and may change during the year. Tokenization’s place in the published agenda nevertheless gives firms a clear reason to expect scrutiny of how their systems operate, as well as what their products promise.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Zymeworks early-stage results on ADC show anti-tumor activity in ovarian cancer
data.description:
Key points:
  • Phase 1 data on Zymeworks' ZW191 found that the folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeting antibody-drug conjugate led to strong anti-tumor activity in ovarian cancer patients that received many prior lines of therapy.
  • In the 6.4 mg/kg dose group, the confirmed objective response rate (cORR) was 64.5% in individuals with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. At the 9.6 mg/kg dose, the figure was 55.3%.
  • cORRs were 69.2% in patients with high FRα expression, 50% in those with intermediate FRα expression, and 55% in individuals with low or negative FRα expression.
  • The disease control rate was, respectively, 100% and 92.1%.
  • In both dosage groups, six-month progression-free survival was 61% in both groups. Median PFS was 7.9 months at 6.4 mg/kg and 9.8 months at 9.6 mg/kg.

data.title: Crypto longs lose $404 million in four hours as bitcoin briefly slips below $80,000
data.description:
Bitcoin briefly dropped below $80,000 on Saturday, and traders with leveraged bets on higher prices took most of the losses. Of the $436.44 million in positions liquidated in the four hours to 1 p.m. ET, $404.15 million were longs, per CoinGlass liquidation data.

Most of the liquidations came in two bursts. Traders saw $208.21 million in longs liquidated in the 15 minutes from 10:15 a.m. ET, as bitcoin (BTC) fell from about $80,640 to $80,100, and another $131.17 million in the 15 minutes from 11:15 a.m., according to CoinGlass.

Long liquidations between 8 a.m. and noon ET totaled $401.91 million. That was the most for any four-hour period since the night of Oct. 14, when $505.57 million in longs were wiped out.

Bitcoin fell to about $79,280 around 11:20 a.m. ET before climbing back to $80,138 by 1 p.m., according to The Block's Bitcoin Price page. As BTC's price recovered, shorts made up $8.35 million of the $10.62 million liquidated in the hour to 1:09 p.m. ET. Bitcoin was down 1.9% over 24 hours, while ether (ETH) was down 3.8% at $2,314.

Liquidations over the past 24 hours came to $815.26 million, up 218% from the previous day, with 201,012 traders hit, per the data. Open interest in crypto futures fell 2.2% to $140.10 billion over the same period. An exchange liquidates a leveraged position when the trader's margin can't cover the losses.

Ether and Hyperliquid

Ether positions accounted for $136.72 million of the four-hour total, against $158.45 million for bitcoin. Ether liquidations totaled $136.72 million, close to bitcoin’s $158.45 million, despite ether currently having only about 18% of bitcoin’s market capitalization.

Longs made up 94.2% of bitcoin liquidations and 92.7% of ether's. The largest single liquidation order of the past 24 hours was an $11.85 million ETH-USDT long on Binance, closed at $2,307.65, per CoinGlass.

Binance accounted for $226.07 million of the four-hour liquidations, 96% of them longs. On Hyperliquid, the onchain perpetual futures exchange, $70.47 million in positions were liquidated, and 99.8% of them were longs, per the data.

Bitcoin ETFs record two days of net outflows

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $137.94 million in net outflows on Friday, according to The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $110.34 million of that, or 80%, and Fidelity's FBTC for $31.78 million, partly offset by $4.19 million in inflows to Morgan Stanley's MSBT.

Friday's outflows came after an even worse day, with the funds logging $635.49 million in net outflows on Thursday. The funds had taken in $1.078 billion from Monday through Wednesday, which left them with $304.73 million in net inflows for the week. The funds held total net assets worth $104.43 billion as of Friday, roughly flat on the week.

Spot ether ETFs had $4.35 million in net inflows on Friday, but those inflows were not enough to offset outflows from earlier in the week, with the funds logging $220.60 million in net outflows over the week. The ether funds have seen net outflows on 14 of 17 trading days in October, totaling $1.175 billion, SoSoValue data show.

Bitcoin also slid on Thursday alongside a sell-off in tech stocks, The Block reported.

Hayes 'dumped it all'

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said early Saturday that he had closed out the directional book at Maelstrom, his family office. "I dumped it all," Hayes wrote on X at 2:18 a.m. ET, adding that he took profits on ETH, ENA, UNI "and other shitcoins."

"I think we gotta go down to go up," Hayes wrote. "It looks a bit dicey out there in macro and geopolitical land." He said he would "sit on the sidelines and wait for the all clear signal."

Hayes did not say which geopolitical risks he meant. The State Department is reducing staff at U.S. embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, the Associated Press reported late Friday. An internal memo cited increased Iranian efforts to target U.S. personnel, according to the AP.

data.title: Pfizer sees strong response for pediatric pneumonia vaccine in mid-stage trial
data.description:
Key points:
  • Data from a phase 2 trial of Pfizer's pediatric 25-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine PF-07872412 (25vPnC) showed that a four-dose series of the candidate provoked a robust immune response against all 25 serotypes.
  • The shot also demonstrated safety and tolerability similar to four doses of Prevnar 20 (pneumococcal 20-valent conjugate vaccine).
  • The study enrolled ~400 full-term infants with the primary objective comparing the safety of PF-07872412 to Prevnar 20. The four-dose series was given at 2, 4, 6, and 12 through 15 months of age.
  • Results showed that local injection site reactions were mild to moderate, with those reactions and systemic events similar between those given PF-07872412 and Prevnar 20.

data.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh meets Yogi Adityanath ahead of PM Modi's Varanasi tour
data.description:
Varanasi, Oct. 24 -- Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in Varanasi on Saturday ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's high-profile visit to the holy city.

On Saturday, Singh visited the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Sankat Mochan Temple and Kaal Bhairav Temple in Varanasi and offered prayers, a day before Prime Minister Narendra Modi's scheduled visit to the city.

Prime Minister Modi is set to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday, October 25, during which he will inaugurate a garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, witness an Indian Air Force aerial display at Namo Ghat and inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar.

At around 11 am, the Prime Minister will inaugurate Arvind Limited's new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, followed by the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat at around 1 pm, where he will attend as the chief guest.

Earlier, Defence Minister Singh on Friday exhorted the Army Commanders to closely monitor geopolitical as well as regional developments and remain prepared for future challenges.

Addressing the Army Commanders' Conference in the national capital, he emphasised the need for a long-term strategic vision spanning the next 20-30 years, and called upon the senior leadership of the Indian Army to remain equally prepared to respond to immediate and emerging challenges.

He stressed that strategies must remain dynamic and flexible, enabling timely adjustments to changing circumstances.

According to the Ministry of Defence, commending the Defence Forces for adapting to evolving operational circumstances, Rajnath Singh highlighted that innovative thinking, enhanced synergy and superior coordination, complemented by advanced weaponry, contributed to the success of Operation Sindoor.

On the other hand, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday held a meeting via video conferencing regarding the PET (Preliminary Eligibility Test) examination scheduled to take place across the state on Sunday.

The Chief Minister joined the meeting from the Varanasi Commissionerate auditorium, while senior officials participated from Lucknow.

During his visit to Varanasi, Adityanath also inspected Namo Ghat.

The Chief Minister's visit comes ahead of the Indian Air Force's Air Show at Varanasi's Namo Ghat on October 25, with preparations underway for the event, which Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend as the chief guest.

He later offered prayers at the Kaal Bhairav Temple and the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in the city.

data.title: Indigo extends Saudi Arabia flight cancellations until Oct 31; Indian Consulate issues detailed advisory for pilgrims
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- IndiGo has extended the cancellation of all its flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam, and Madinah until Saturday, October 31, in view of the evolving security situation in Saudi Arabia.

The airline confirmed the decision in a travel advisory, emphasising that passenger and crew safety remain its top priorities as it coordinates with relevant authorities.

"Following a careful assessment, flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will also remain cancelled until 31 October 2026 (inclusive)," the airline stated in a post on X.

"The safety and well-being of our customers and crew continue to guide every decision we make. We remain in close coordination with the relevant authorities to ensure safe operations," IndiGo added.

This came a day after the airline announced that the flights "to and from Riyadh will remain cancelled until 31 October 2026 (inclusive), while flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain cancelled until 27 October 2026 (inclusive)."

Amplifying the announcement, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia wrote in a post on X, "Indigo flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain cancelled until 31 October 2026."

On Friday, Akasa Air also extended the suspension of its flights to and from Jeddah until November 10 and Riyadh until November 30 amid the evolving security situation in Saudi Arabia, the airline said in a travel update on Friday.

Responding to the widespread flight disruptions, the Consulate General of India in Jeddah issued a detailed advisory to support Indian nationals, particularly Umrah pilgrims affected by cancellations.

The consulate stated that it is actively extending assistance through its round-the-clock control rooms operational in Jeddah and Makkah. Supported by local Indian community associations and volunteers, the mission is facilitating food, essential medicines, and immediate relief wherever required.

Consular officials confirmed ongoing coordination with Saudi government authorities, including the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah as well as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to resolve challenges regarding visa validity extensions and delayed departures.

"Umrah pilgrims facing difficulties relating to accommodation or other services during their extended stay may also contact the Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah's Pilgrim Care Centre at 1966 (accessible within Saudi Arabia) to register their concerns and obtain a case reference number," the consulate advised, adding that pilgrims should share their reference numbers with consular control rooms for further follow-up.

The diplomatic mission is also maintaining continuous contact with Indian airlines regarding passenger refunds and connecting Indian Umrah tour operators with airlines that continue to operate flights to India. These alternative travel arrangements remain subject to seat availability, applicable airfares, and specific airline guidelines.

The consulate urged all affected travellers to remain in regular communication with their respective airlines, travel agents, and Umrah service providers for rebooking and refund processes, confirming that it continues to work with all stakeholders to facilitate the early return of stranded Indian nationals.

Earlier in the day, Saudi authorities issued an emergency alert warning of a "hostile aerial threat" in the city of Mecca, with the danger later reported to have passed.

The General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defence issued a warning in Mecca Province to alert residents of a potential danger.

In a post on X, it said, "A warning has been issued by the National Early Warning Platform in Mecca Province to alert of a potential danger."

In another post on X, it said later, " Alert: The danger has passed in Mecca Province."

Saudi authorities also issued alerts for Jeddah, Yanbu and Taif governorates, subsequently confirming that the danger had passed in these areas.

In its alerts, the Saudi Civil Defence urged residents to continue following safety instructions and avoid gatherings and filming. Authorities also advised people to call 911 in case of an emergency.

Meanwhile, the spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, Major General Turki Al-Malki, said air defences had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi militia towards the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu.

The development comes amid heightened security concerns in the region, with attacks targeting civilian and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Friday said the Indian Embassy and Consulate in Saudi Arabia were actively coordinating with airlines and tour operators to facilitate the return of Indian pilgrims stranded in the country.

data.title: BJP leader Kirit Somaiya holds Jail Bharo Satyagraha over alleged unauthorised mosque near Mumbai airport
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 24 -- BJP leader Kirit Somaiya on Saturday held a Jail Bharo Satyagraha, demanding removal of an alleged unauthorised mosque near Mumbai airport.

Speaking to ANI, Somaiya declared that the Terminal 2 mosque must be demolished, as ordered by the MMRDA and the Maharashtra government.

The BJP leader further announced that if the police do not arrest Mohammad Sarwar, he will sit at the police station until an FIR is registered over the matter.

"... The Terminal 2 mosque must be demolished, as ordered by the MMRDA and the Maharashtra government. Today, around 100 of my supporters and I have come here." said Somaiya.

The protest took place amid escalating tensions surrounding a mosque situated near Terminal 2 of Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport.

The tensions intensified after the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) on September 10 declared the structure unauthorised and directed the airport operator, Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL), to take appropriate steps for its removal in accordance with due process.

This directive came following a complaint received by the MMRDA concerning the facility located near the VIP arrival and taxi stand area of Terminal 2.

In the wake of the development, Somaiya asserted that if swift measures are not taken, he will personally proceed to demolish the structure.

Meanwhile, AIMIM leader Waris Pathan demanded legal action against Kirit Somaiya, stating that his party has requested the police commissioner to take cognisance of the matter. He also demanded the registration of an FIR against the BJP leader.

"A controversy was stirred over the mosque outside Mumbai International Airport Terminal Two. People had been offering namaz there for years. Suddenly, these hateful BJP workers, Kirit Somaiya, came along with nothing better to do and claimed it was an illegal encroachment.

They spoke to the trustees, who filed a case in court and sent a notice to the MMRDA... The whole matter is sub judice, and amidst this, Kirit Somaiya went there yesterday with some goons and staged a sit-in protest... Then they went there and threatened everyone, saying that they will bring a hammer within 48 hours and demolish the mosque... Why isn't there a case against him?..." said Pathan.

data.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Q2 standalone profit rises 29% to Rs 4,212 crore; net interest margin narrows
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 24 -- Kotak Mahindra Bank on Saturday reported a 29 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 4,212 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 3,253 crore in the corresponding period last year, even as its net interest margin declined during the quarter.

According to the bank's unaudited financial results filed with the stock exchanges, consolidated profit after tax rose 26 per cent to Rs 5,645 crore from Rs 4,468 crore a year earlier.

Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 16 per cent year-on-year to Rs 8,459 crore from Rs 7,311 crore.

However, the bank's net interest margin (NIM), a key indicator of lending profitability, narrowed to 4.31 per cent from 4.54 per cent in the year-ago quarter and 4.53 per cent in the preceding quarter.

"The moderation in NIM was largely on account of FCNR(B) mobilisation during the quarter," the bank said in its earnings release.

During the quarter, the bank mobilised approximately Rs 55,344 crore in Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits and provided loans aggregating to around Rs 16,110 crore through its international branches.

The large foreign currency deposit inflows also contributed to the bank's headline growth in advances and deposits.

Net advances increased 25 per cent year-on-year to Rs 5,77,295 crore as of September 30, 2026. However, excluding loans against FCNR(B) deposits and the loan portfolio acquired from Kotak Mahindra Investments, advances grew 19 per cent.

Similarly, total deposits rose 23 per cent to Rs 6,51,491 crore, but growth stood at 13 per cent excluding FCNR(B) deposits.

The bank's current account and savings account (CASA) ratio declined to 38.2 per cent from 42.3 per cent a year ago. Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, the ratio stood at 41.8 per cent.

On asset quality, the bank reported an improvement, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 1.04 per cent from 1.39 per cent a year earlier, while net NPA fell to 0.24 per cent from 0.32 per cent.

Slippages declined 24 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,230 crore, while provisions fell 15 per cent to Rs 803 crore.

The bank's operating profit increased 21 per cent year-on-year to Rs 6,382 crore, supported by higher interest income and a 21 per cent rise in fees and services income to Rs 2,926 crore.

The results indicate stronger earnings and improved asset quality, although the moderation in lending margins and the difference between reported and adjusted balance-sheet growth remain important indicators to watch in the coming quarters.

data.title: PM Modi to inaugurate RBI data centre in Bhubaneswar, garment facility in Varanasi on October 25
data.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday, October 25, to inaugurate a garment manufacturing unit in Varanasi, attend an Indian Air Force aerial display along the Ganges and open the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, according to an official press release.

Modi's engagements will begin at around 11 am in Varanasi, where he will inaugurate Arvind Limited's newly established garment manufacturing facility. The unit is expected to boost the textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem, encourage industrial expansion and generate employment, particularly for women.

The facility will adopt modern manufacturing practices and cater to a global customer base, enabling garments produced in Varanasi to reach international markets, the release stated. The project is also expected to reinforce Uttar Pradesh's position as an industrial investment destination and support manufacturing-driven economic growth.

The initiative, which will predominantly involve women, also reflects the emphasis on women-led development, according to the release.

IAF aerial display at Namo Ghat

At around 1 pm, the Prime Minister will attend the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi as the chief guest. The event, organised to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force (IAF), will be held under the theme "Wings over Ganges".

The display will feature several combat aircraft, including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, SU-30MKI and Rafale, alongside transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also take part, highlighting jointness in military operations.

The IAF's leading display formations, including the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will demonstrate precision flying, coordination and operational excellence during the programme, the press release said.

Following his engagements in Uttar Pradesh, Modi will travel to Odisha for the inauguration of the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar at approximately 4.45 pm. He will also address the gathering.

RBI data centre to strengthen financial infrastructure

The newly developed facilities are intended to enhance the technological infrastructure supporting India's financial system by establishing a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing environment for the RBI and the wider financial sector.

The complex will house four advanced data centres to accommodate critical payment and settlement systems, as well as other flagship initiatives. It has received Tier IV certification from the Uptime Institute, a global benchmark for data centre infrastructure, placing it in the highest category of operational resilience.

According to the release, the facility ranks among the world's largest Tier IV-certified installations in the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector.

The infrastructure is expected to improve the accessibility, efficiency and dependability of digital financial services while providing a secure technological base for India's increasingly digital financial economy. It is also expected to strengthen the RBI's standing in digital infrastructure among central banks.

The accompanying Cybersecurity Training Institute will offer specialised training, research and capability-building programmes in cybersecurity and enterprise technology for the financial sector.

Its focus areas will include emerging and advanced technologies relevant to the BFSI industry, such as quantum computing and artificial intelligence, the release added.

data.title: Hyperliquid Strategies Expands PURR Stock Buyback As HYPE Extends Monthly Losses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Hyperliquid’s token edged lower on Saturday, a day after Hyperliquid Strategies more than tripled its stock buyback program to $100 million.
  • PURR stock closed up over 1% on Friday, while HYPE has fallen over 19% in the past month.
  • CME Group CEO Terry Duffy raised concerns about Hyperliquid’s lack of know-your-customer checks and the risks of automatic liquidations.

Hyperliquid (HYPE) edged lower on Saturday, even after its treasury company, Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR), more than tripled its stock buyback program to $100 million.

Hyperliquid Strategies said on Friday that its board approved raising its stock repurchase program from $30 million to up to $100 million. About $72 million remained available under the expanded authorization, which meant that the company had already used roughly $28 million. The program's end date also moved from December 5, 2026, to October 31, 2027.

The company said the increase reflected the “Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy." Hyperliquid Strategies is "currently the largest HYPE-focused digital asset treasury vehicle." Among the risks it listed in its announcement, it said its stock price "will be highly correlated to the price of HYPE tokens."

HYPE Slides As PURR Stock Gains

Hyperliquid Strategies held about 38.8 million HYPE tokens, worth roughly $2.9 billion, according to its treasury dashboard.

PURR stock closed up over 1% on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around PURR was also in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

In contrast, HYPE’s price was down over 2% over the past 24 hours. Over the past month, HYPE has fallen over 19%, posting a stark contrast from last month, when HYPE posted an all-time high of $97.96, over a month ago. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around HYPE remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

However, HYPE was up over 197% so far this year.

CME CEO Raises KYC Concerns

Hyperliquid also faced questions about how it would operate in the U.S. after CME Group CEO Terry Duffy said that Hyperliquid was “basically the plumbing” and that its users should carry the regulatory burden. Speaking on Bloomberg’s Odd Lots podcast on Tuesday, Duffy said, “don't know because there's no KYC. We don't know who they are. So there's a lot of violation of U.S. law for him to deploy what he was suggesting to manage” on the rival firm.

He also warned about automatic liquidations on highly leveraged products. Duffy said such positions “can cascade and create market-moving events because of the high leverage and the small amount of dollars.”

Duffy’s comments came a day before CME reported $1.7 billion in revenue, its highest for a third quarter on record. “Our average daily volume reached 29.4 million contracts, the highest Q3 ADV on record,” Duffy said. On the earnings call, he pointed to “the strong traction of our 24/7 cryptocurrency products launched earlier this year.”

data.title: Bitcoin Hashrate Reclaims One Zettahash As Mining Competition Rebounds
data.description:
TL;DR: BlocksBridge reported Bitcoin’s seven-day hashrate above one zettahash in the week to October 22. Mining competition has recovered despite companies shifting some infrastructure toward AI.

A mining company can switch strategy without making Bitcoin mining any easier for the businesses that remain. New network data puts that distinction in focus.

In its October 22 Miner Weekly report, BlocksBridge Consulting said the network’s seven-day average hashrate had recovered above one zettahash per second, its highest level since March 3. One zettahash is equivalent to 1,000 exahashes per second.

The report also recorded a 5.92% increase in mining difficulty on October 16. Together, the figures show that announcements about individual operators leaving mining cannot be treated as a direct measure of network-wide competition.

A Mining Exit Does Not Necessarily Remove The Machines

BlocksBridge’s analysis separates a site’s future use from the fate of the equipment installed there. A facility can shift toward AI infrastructure while Bitcoin mining machines are sold or relocated, allowing them to contribute computing power elsewhere.

That distinction does not establish where every additional unit of hashrate came from. It does explain why corporate announcements and network data can point in different directions without contradicting each other.

For an operator that keeps mining, the relevant competitive field is the worldwide network. A rival’s strategic exit only reduces that field if the associated computing capacity actually disappears and is not offset by activity elsewhere.

The same caution applies to expansion plans. Announced capacity, installed machines and equipment actively submitting work are different stages. Only the last contributes to observed network performance.

Hashrate, Difficulty And Revenue Measure Different Things

A hashrate figure is an estimate of computational work, not a direct meter reading from every miner. Blockchain.com’s chart methodology explains that estimates use block production and difficulty; short periods can fluctuate because finding blocks involves randomness. A seven-day average helps smooth that noise.

That is why the time window matters. The reported one-zettahash milestone refers to a seven-day average through the October 22 report, not a guaranteed reading at every moment since then or a separate 30-day measure.

Mining difficulty is the protocol’s adjustment to the work required to find a block. The Bitcoin developer documentation describes a recalculation every 2,016 blocks, targeting roughly two weeks for that interval. Faster block production generally leads to a harder target for the next period.

Revenue is another question. More network computing power does not automatically mean more income for each machine. With other conditions unchanged, an operator supplying the same amount of work faces a smaller relative share when competing capacity expands.

Profitability also depends on the value of block rewards and fees, power costs and equipment efficiency. A rise in Bitcoin hashrate therefore cannot, by itself, establish whether a miner’s margins improved.

The rebound is evidence of renewed network competition over the reported period. Its commercial significance rests on who can supply that work economically, rather than on whether a prominent company has changed its strategy.
